notes: Breadboard hole naming follows the catalogue convention (rows f-j = bank 'b', rows a-e = bank 't'), using the row letters printed on the breadboard in the circuit image. The image's upper half is labelled j-f, so it maps to bank 'b'.
The pushbutton straddles the centre gap in columns 4 and 6: side 1 in 4b.f/6b.f and side 2 in 4t.e/6t.e. The button's two sides are bridged only when it is pressed.

The blue wire runs from Leonardo pin 2 to 6b.i, which is on the button's side 1. The black wire runs from the first GND pin (GND.1, next to 5V) to 4t.c, which is on side 2. Pressing the button connects pin 2 to GND.
No external resistor is used. The sketch enables INPUT_PULLUP on pin 2.
The manual says the Leonardo, Micro or Due can be used. The circuit image shows a Leonardo, so that is what I used.
